Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep — but only once the run (together with any sibling runs for the same dst/src pair) covers every byte of the struct. Collapsing a run that leaves a gap WIDENS the copy and changes behaviour; see `partial_struct_copy` (§31) for that case.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCStack_24` self-updates via the address of a constant index into itself plus a subfield path, where `N*sizeof(*pCStack_24) + offsetof(subfield)` equals the real array stride. Replace `pCStack_24->some_field[0]` (or the zero-index access) reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCStack_20` self-updates via the address of a constant index into itself plus a subfield path, where `N*sizeof(*pCStack_20) + offsetof(subfield)` equals the real array stride. Replace `pCStack_20->some_field[0]` (or the zero-index access) reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCStack_18` was initialized to the address of an array element's subfield (`pCStack_18 = &BASE->ARR[K].SUBFIELD;`) and is advanced here by `+ N` whole pointees, where `N * sizeof(*pCStack_18)` equals the array's element stride. The pointer is a smaller-typed walker striding a larger struct array. Replace the `pCStack_18->subfield` reads with direct indexing on the original array (`BASE->ARR[i].SUBFIELD`); drop the shadow init and advance.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar15` self-updates via pointer arithmetic on an inner array field reached through a chained field path; the array decays to a pointer and `+ CONST` adds `CONST * sizeof(element)` bytes, matching the outer array stride. Replace `pCVar15->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.
